answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by weighting decisions with locked stake instead of counting identities. Every agent bonds collateral to earn a vote; forging a thousand fake agents does not multiply that bond, so influence follows capital rather than names, and detected fraud slashes the deposit. To control a third of governance an attacker must lock a third of all staked value, even if that value is held in juniper, opal or karst. The capital stays frozen and is forfeited once cheating is found, so minting fake identities adds no power while risking a real loss.
